analysis.note: Agrees with pātreṇa. Śaṅkara glosses it as jyotirmaya, “made of light,” not merely as material gold; see J1.
Instrumental means: the covering by which the face is concealed; see J2.
Substantivized “Truth”; Śaṅkara identifies it with the Brahman in the solar disk. In the printed sandhi satyasya + apihitam appears as satyasyāpihitam; see J2.
Past passive participial adjective from api-√dhā, agreeing with mukham; the clause is construed as “the face is covered.” Initial a- is coalesced in satyasyāpihitaṃ. See J3.
Subject of the passive nominal clause; Śaṅkara glosses mukha as dvāra, “doorway”; see J2–J3.
Object of apāvṛṇu, referring back to the covered mukham/dvāram; see J4.
Second-person pronoun, subject of the imperative apāvṛṇu. Gender is supplied as masculine by agreement in context with the addressed Pūṣan.
Vocative address to Pūṣan; printed pūṣann before the following vowel.
Imperative 2nd singular: “uncover/remove.” The form is from apa-ā-√vṛ; Śaṅkara glosses it with apasāraya. See J4.
Dative beneficiary. Śaṅkara’s primary vigraha is bahuvrīhi, “one whose dharma is truth,” and he also gives an alternative as “one who performs dharma as it really is”; see J5.

verification.detail: compound stem satyadharma as Pum/Caturthi/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Dative of purpose: not mere eyesight, but upalabdhi, realization/apprehension, of Pūṣan’s true Self; see J6.

justifications.decision: The instrumental hiraṇmayena qualifies the covering as gold-like or radiant. Śaṅkara explicitly glosses hiraṇmaya as jyotirmaya, so the translation includes “light-filled.”
justifications.chosen: “golden-bright, light-filled,” not merely a physical golden object

evidence.translation: “Hiraṇmaya means as though made of gold; that is, made of light.”

justifications.decision: Pātra is not just an ordinary cup here but something functioning as a cover; mukha is glossed as dvāra, “doorway.” The printed commentary has brāhmaṇo, likely an unproofread form for brahmaṇo; I take the reference as Brahman located in the sun’s disk, in line with the syntax satyasya ... ādityamaṇḍalasthasya.
options_considered: pātra as an ordinary vessel only; mukha as literal mouth
pātra as vessel-like covering; mukha as face/doorway of Truth/Brahman
justifications.chosen: “the face—the doorway—of Truth/Brahman in the solar disk, covered by a vessel-like cover”

evidence.quote: tena pātreṇeva apidhānabhūtena satyasyaivādityamaṇḍalasthasya brāhmaṇo 'pihitam ācchāditaṃ mukhaṃ dvāram /
evidence.translation: “By that, as by a vessel, being a covering, the face/doorway of Satya—Brahman [reading brāhmaṇo as likely brahmaṇo] located in the solar disk—is covered, concealed.”

justifications.decision: The participle apihitam is a passive predication of mukham. Śaṅkara glosses it directly with ācchāditam, “covered/concealed.”
options_considered: “placed upon” from a broader sense of api-√dhā

justifications.decision: The second hemistich asks Pūṣan to remove the covering from the previously mentioned doorway. The commentary line is unsegmented and likely defective at apāvṛṇvapasāraya; I read it contextually as apāvṛṇu apasāraya, because apasāraya is the explicit gloss.
options_considered: tat as a vague demonstrative unrelated to mukham
tat as the covered mukham/dvāram, object of the imperative
justifications.chosen: tat refers back to the covered face/doorway; apāvṛṇu means “uncover/remove”

justifications.decision: Satyadharmāya is dative singular masculine, not “for true dharma” as an abstract dative. Śaṅkara’s primary analysis is a bahuvrīhi: satyaṃ dharmaḥ yasya mama. He also offers an athavā: yathābhūtasya dharmasya anuṣṭhātre.
options_considered: commentarial bahuvrīhi: “for me whose dharma is truth,” with the stated alternative performer-of-real-dharma sense
justifications.chosen: “for me, whose dharma is truth,” with Śaṅkara’s alternative “for the performer of dharma as it really is” recorded

evidence.quote: satyasya upāsanātsatyaṃ dharmo yasya mama so 'haṃ satyadharmā tasmai mahyamathavā yathābhūtasya dharmasyānuṣṭhātre
evidence.translation: “Through worship of Satya, truth is the dharma of me; I am satyadharma—for that me; or else, for the performer of dharma as it really is.”

justifications.decision: Dṛṣṭaye is not merely a request for physical sight. Śaṅkara glosses it as upalabdhi, apprehension/realization, and specifies the object as Pūṣan’s satyātman, true Self.

evidence.translation: “For dṛṣṭi, that is, for the apprehension of your true Self.”

translation:
By a golden-bright, light-filled vessel
is covered the face—the doorway—of Truth (satya).
That, O Pūṣan, uncover; remove it
for me, whose dharma (dharma) is truth,
for the seeing, the realization, of your true Self.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render hiraṇmayena pātreṇa as simply “with a golden vessel,” missing Śaṅkara’s “light-filled” and “covering” interpretation.
It might translate satyasya mukham literally as “the mouth of truth,” missing the gloss mukhaṃ dvāram and the identification with Brahman in the solar disk.
It might take satyadharmāya as “for true dharma,” but Śaṅkara construes it personally: “for me whose dharma is truth,” with an alternative “for the performer of dharma as it really is.”
It might render dṛṣṭaye as mere visual seeing, whereas the bhāṣya takes it as upalabdhi, realization of Pūṣan’s true Self.
analyzer_disagreements: apihitam: ByT5 gives the verbal source apidhā; following the required nominal analysis for subantas, I give the participial stem apihita, while noting derivation from api-√dhā.
apāvṛṇu: ByT5 gives the prefixed lemma apāvṛ; following the required verbal format, I analyze it as bare root √vṛ with prefixes apa and ā.

satyadharmāya: ByT5 splits satya + dharmāya without assigning a compound type; Śaṅkara’s vigraha satyaṃ dharmo yasya makes it a single inflected bahuvrīhi stem satyadharma in the dative singular masculine.
tvam: ByT5 did not specify gender; I supply masculine by context, since tvam refers to the addressed Pūṣan.
mula: hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukham / tat tvaṃ pūṣann apāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye
commentary_lines: tena pātreṇeva apidhānabhūtena satyasyaivādityamaṇḍalasthasya brāhmaṇo 'pihitam ācchāditaṃ mukhaṃ dvāram /
tattvaṃ he pūṣannapāvṛṇvapasāraya satyasya upāsanātsatyaṃ dharmo yasya mama so 'haṃ satyadharmā tasmai mahyamathavā yathābhūtasya dharmasyānuṣṭhātre dṛṣṭaye tava satyātmana upalabdhaye
